text:
Support Ops: FYI escalation from ACME — they see intermittent 429s + a billing spike yesterday. Said traffic is bursty (backend fan-out) and they share a single API key across workers. Billing shows a ~3x token charge during the window. Can someone help repro and recommend sane defaults?

Kevin: Can you paste a sample log snippet or the X-RateLimit headers they saw? Also did they use streaming or non-streaming calls? :eyes:

Support Ops: here's the relevant log line from our proxy: `2025-11-03T14:22:18Z level=warn client_key=sk-acme*** rate_limiter=reject reason=token_bucket_empty global_quota_left=0 request_id=rc_01F…`  No streaming, simple text gen. They reported `x-ratelimit-limit`/`x-ratelimit-remaining` inconsistent with dashboard.

Maya: quick repro loop I used locally to mimic their fanout (single key, 50 concurrent processes, each doing ~5 req/s for 60s):
```bash
# simple stress by parallel curl (non-streaming)
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  (for j in $(seq 1 300); do
    curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme123"
      -H "Content-Type: application/json"
      -d '{"input":"hello"}'
      https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate > /dev/null;
    sleep 0.2
  done) &
done; wait
```
This gives a bursty pattern with short inter-request delays; reproduced `429` spikes and saw `x-ratelimit-reset` moving forward unexpectedly.

Jen: OK. Two quick things: (1) per-key windowing vs per-customer aggregate matters here — ACME's infra shares 1 key across many hosts -> single key throttle. (2) billing spike usually from retries/backoff loops doubling requests or from client-side fanout counting tokens multiple times.

Jen: Proposed internal test plan to pick sane defaults (lets keep it tight and measurable):
- env: staging-ratebench (mirrors prod routing, but no billing auth)
- axes: per-key RPM, per-key TPM, per-project (global) TPM, burst_capacity (tokens allowed above steady-state for 10s)
- baseline scenario: 10 clients, 5 concurrency each, steady 10 req/s per client for 5m
- burst scenario: ramp to 200 req/s for 30s, then back to baseline
- multi-key scenario: 10 keys, same workload to measure aggregate effects
- metrics: 429 rate, p95 latency, token_consumed/sec, x-ratelimit-* header consistency
- target "sane defaults" to evaluate: start at 120 RPM, 6k TPM, burst_capacity = 40 (per-key).
Please run 3 repeats and attach artifacts (grafana panel + raw logs).

Kevin: 120 RPM / 6k TPM is reasonable but let's also test a conservative default at 60 RPM / 3k TPM for low-tier customers. We should capture how burst_capacity maps to Retry-After behavior.

Alex: Notes from runtime side: our token-bucket refill interval is 1s and we have a short-circuit global quota we hit when a tenant exhausts monthly commit. Two suggestions:
- increase burst token cap by +50% for short windows (10-30s) for customer keys that show legitimate fan-out patterns
- emit `x-ratelimit-suggested-backoff` header when we hit soft-throttle so clients can switch to queued retry vs immediate retry
Also add a rehitrate flag in the rate-limiter logs so we can see per-request decision path.

SRE Bot: Created bench job: https://ci.internal/jobs/bench/rs-4821 (staging-ratebench) — queued. Ticket #INC-2025-563 linked.

Support Ops: Thanks — will coordinate with ACME for scheduled test window (they prefer PST morning). I'll run Jen's matrix in staging once the job finishes and paste graphs here. :thumbsup:

Kevin: if results show >1% 429 in baseline, we should lower default RPM for self-serve and recommend Dedicated capacity for high fan-out workloads.

Maya: one gotcha we observed: some client libraries retry on any 5xx/429 with no jitter -> multiplies load. I'll add a sample retry snippet to our docs to encourage exponential backoff + jitter.

Support Ops: action items captured:
- Jen to execute test matrix and upload artifacts (start: 1837658000)
- Alex to add log flag and header proposal (PR link when ready)
- Support to schedule ACME test window and validate client retry patterns
- SRE Bot job will run and post results here

Support Ops: closing for now, will reopen thread once we have bench artifacts. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
